effectAssertions: The exact disposable workspace has zero total and online agent identities plus zero total and live Fleet node records before allocation.
negativeAssertions: Ambient Daytona resources and pre-existing Relay identities cannot be claimed or deleted by this run.
clean-baseline.lifecycleAssertion: Baseline inventory is captured before the first ownership intent.
clean-baseline.teardownAssertion: The same baseline identities and exact owned-resource absence are checked after cleanup.
clean-baseline.retryAssertion: Malformed or truncated inventory is a failure, never an empty baseline.

effectAssertions: An exact named Daytona sandbox, Fleet node, worker, initial MCP sentinel, placement, and runtime binary attestation are observed.
negativeAssertions: No production/fallback snapshot, pre-existing sandbox, wrong node, or unconfirmed worker can pass.
board-provision.lifecycleAssertion: Provisioning, readiness, and initial response use monotonic timing and bounded timeouts.
board-provision.teardownAssertion: The worker identity and exact sandbox ID are owned and must be absent at campaign cleanup.
board-provision.retryAssertion: An uncertain create is reconciled by exact nonce-bound name before cleanup; duplicate ownership is rejected.

effectAssertions: Both board sandboxes, Fleet node IDs, creation times, snapshot IDs, manifests, and runtime binaries are distinct/current as required.
negativeAssertions: Reused sandbox IDs, reused node IDs, stale creation times, mutable snapshots, and runtime digest drift fail.
distinct-topology.lifecycleAssertion: Topology is checked after both nodes are ready and before board commands execute.
distinct-topology.teardownAssertion: Both exact sandbox IDs remain in the owned-resource ledger for final absence checks.
distinct-topology.retryAssertion: A partial topology remains failed or blocked; one node cannot stand in for two.

effectAssertions: The initially spawned worker posts its unique MCP sentinel from the requested node.
negativeAssertions: Dispatch text without the exact sender-bound sentinel is not readiness proof.
initial-injection.lifecycleAssertion: The response is bounded by the provision sentinel deadline.
initial-injection.teardownAssertion: The initial worker is released and its identity is reconciled later in the same attempt.
initial-injection.retryAssertion: A missing sentinel stays failed; the other node cannot satisfy it.

effectAssertions: The public Fleet leaf returns parseable state containing the exact owned nodes or agents requested by its filter.
negativeAssertions: An empty, malformed, truncated, degraded, or wrong-node result cannot pass.
fleet-read.lifecycleAssertion: The read is monotonic-timed and bounded.
fleet-read.teardownAssertion: Read-only; owned resources are covered by campaign cleanup.
fleet-read.retryAssertion: Any internal command retry must still return one complete authoritative result.

effectAssertions: The exact worker is observed in live Fleet placement on the requested node, posts its sender-bound sentinel, and preserves supplied invocation metadata.
negativeAssertions: Echoing the requested node, dispatch acknowledgement, or a sentinel from a differently placed identity cannot pass.
targeted-fleet-spawn.lifecycleAssertion: Dispatch, placement confirmation, sentinel response, release, and absence are bounded and timed.
targeted-fleet-spawn.teardownAssertion: Each worker process is absent and its nonce-owned identity is deleted before its node is reused.
targeted-fleet-spawn.retryAssertion: Same-name or ambiguous dispatch cannot create a second live worker; exact placement is re-read after dispatch.

effectAssertions: Automatic placement selects one of the two owned candidate nodes and the exact worker posts its sentinel.
negativeAssertions: Placement on an ambient workspace node or an unplaced roster identity fails.
automatic-fleet-spawn.lifecycleAssertion: Placement and response are confirmed before support cleanup.
automatic-fleet-spawn.teardownAssertion: The exact automatically placed identity is released and removed.
automatic-fleet-spawn.retryAssertion: The owned-node allowlist is authoritative across placement retries.

effectAssertions: The named provider launches on its requested candidate node and the exact worker posts a sender-bound MCP sentinel.
negativeAssertions: Capability advertisement or dispatch alone is insufficient; wrong-provider, wrong-node, and immediate-exit workers fail.
provider-spawn.lifecycleAssertion: Readiness and response use bounded timeouts and monotonic timing.
provider-spawn.teardownAssertion: Every provider worker is released and its identity reconciled before node reuse.
provider-spawn.retryAssertion: Transient confirmation may retry inside the product, but the board records one final exact outcome.

effectAssertions: The public command rejects the invalid invocation with the required stable diagnostic.
negativeAssertions: The rejected request creates no owned agent, node, or sandbox.
expected-rejection.teardownAssertion: No resource cleanup is necessary because creation must not start.
expected-rejection.retryAssertion: Retrying the same invalid input remains side-effect free.

effectAssertions: Root Relayfile mounting reaches readiness, materializes both exact marker hashes, launches the worker, and returns its sentinel.
negativeAssertions: HTTP/CPU timeout, partial materialization, unknown outcome, wrong data plane, and stranded sandbox all fail.
sandbox-root-mount.lifecycleAssertion: Provision, mount readiness, worker confirmation, and response are bounded and timed.
sandbox-root-mount.teardownAssertion: The root-probe worker and exact sandbox must be absent after cleanup.
sandbox-root-mount.retryAssertion: Checkpoint/retry may resume but cannot duplicate the sandbox or silently omit files.

effectAssertions: The included marker hash exists, the excluded root-only marker is absent, and the worker responds from the scoped mount.
negativeAssertions: A root mount, excluded-file leak, partial mount, or wrong candidate/data plane fails.
sandbox-scoped-mount.lifecycleAssertion: Scoped readiness and response are bounded and timed.
sandbox-scoped-mount.teardownAssertion: Releasing the final worker must reclaim the exact owned sandbox within the release SLO.
sandbox-scoped-mount.retryAssertion: Repeated scope reconciliation cannot widen the requested path set.

effectAssertions: A no-mount sandbox launches the worker and both Relayfile marker paths remain absent.
negativeAssertions: Implicit Relayfile provisioning or materialization fails the control.
sandbox-no-mount.lifecycleAssertion: Sandbox and worker readiness are bounded and timed.
sandbox-no-mount.teardownAssertion: The no-mount worker and exact sandbox must be absent after cleanup.
sandbox-no-mount.retryAssertion: Provision retries preserve the explicit no-mount contract.

effectAssertions: Release stops the exact worker process and preserves or deletes its identity according to the selected flag.
negativeAssertions: Acknowledgement without process absence, incorrect identity semantics, or node contamination fails.
release-process.lifecycleAssertion: Release and exact process/identity reconciliation are bounded and timed.
release-process.teardownAssertion: Support cleanup removes any identity intentionally preserved by the command under test.
release-process.retryAssertion: Repeated cleanup is idempotent and cannot target a non-owned identity.

effectAssertions: Releasing the final sandbox worker deletes or reclaims its exact sandbox within the bounded poll.
negativeAssertions: A zero-agent sandbox left started or merely scheduled for 24-hour deletion fails.
release-sandbox.lifecycleAssertion: Release-to-sandbox-absence duration is measured against the short reclaim window.
release-sandbox.teardownAssertion: Final cleanup re-verifies the exact sandbox remains absent.
release-sandbox.retryAssertion: Reconciliation is exact-name/id based and repeated deletion is idempotent.

effectAssertions: Fleet policy returns an explicit nullable override and boolean effective value.
negativeAssertions: Missing SDK support, malformed schema, or an unknown initial override fails.
fleet-policy-read.lifecycleAssertion: The policy read is bounded and timed.
fleet-policy-read.teardownAssertion: Read-only; the captured value becomes the exact restoration target for mutation probes.
fleet-policy-read.retryAssertion: A retry must converge on the same authoritative override.

effectAssertions: The authorized disposable workspace reads back the exact requested override.
negativeAssertions: Wrong workspace identity, missing authorization, failed readback, or failed exact restoration cannot pass.
fleet-policy-mutation.lifecycleAssertion: Each mutation/readback and final restoration is bounded and timed.
fleet-policy-mutation.teardownAssertion: The original nullable override is restored in finally and independently verified.
fleet-policy-mutation.retryAssertion: Read-after-write makes repeated mutation idempotent and observable.

effectAssertions: The node-local public leaf returns parseable, exact state for the owned node or worker requested.
negativeAssertions: Host fallback, Daytona warning-only output, malformed JSON, or wrong-agent data cannot pass.
node-read.lifecycleAssertion: The read is bounded and monotonic-timed.
node-read.teardownAssertion: Read-only; owned resources are handled by campaign cleanup.
node-read.retryAssertion: A retried read must remain bound to the same exact sandbox ID.

effectAssertions: The exact broker stream emits bytes containing the unique triggered sentinel for the named worker.
negativeAssertions: Timeout, stderr warnings, unrelated worker bytes, or an empty stream cannot pass.
node-stream.lifecycleAssertion: Subscription, trigger, and bounded stream termination are timed.
node-stream.teardownAssertion: The stream process group is terminated and the worker remains under owned cleanup.
node-stream.retryAssertion: Reconnect behavior cannot substitute cached or unrelated output.

effectAssertions: The requested provider/runtime/model/channel configuration appears in node inventory and the exact worker posts its MCP sentinel.
negativeAssertions: CLI exit zero without sustained inventory plus sentinel evidence fails.
direct-node-spawn.lifecycleAssertion: Spawn, inventory, response, release, and absence are bounded and timed.
direct-node-spawn.teardownAssertion: Each worker process and Relay identity are reconciled before node reuse.
direct-node-spawn.retryAssertion: A failed or ambiguous spawn is reconciled through exact identity lookup, never assumed absent.

effectAssertions: The task worker posts its exact sentinel and then exits without an explicit release.
negativeAssertions: Sentinel without exit, exit without sentinel, or a lingering process fails.
task-exit-spawn.lifecycleAssertion: Task completion and process absence are bounded and timed.
task-exit-spawn.teardownAssertion: The remaining Relay identity is removed exactly.
task-exit-spawn.retryAssertion: The same lifecycle cannot leave duplicate or reusable live processes.

effectAssertions: The control command reports and demonstrates its requested model, terminal, or delivery-mode effect against the exact worker.
negativeAssertions: Accepted/pending-only receipts, wrong streams, premature injection, or unread messages fail.
agent-control.lifecycleAssertion: Control, readback, injection, and response are bounded and timed.
agent-control.teardownAssertion: The controlled worker is released and reconciled after all controls.
agent-control.retryAssertion: Readback and message-reader receipts make retries observable and duplicate-safe.

effectAssertions: Direct release proves process absence and the exact same name can subsequently launch and respond once.
negativeAssertions: Release acknowledgement with a lingering process or duplicate same-name workers fails.
node-release-reclaim.lifecycleAssertion: Release, absence, reclaim spawn, response, and second release are bounded and timed.
node-release-reclaim.teardownAssertion: The reclaimed worker and identity are absent before leaving the control sequence.
node-release-reclaim.retryAssertion: Same-name reuse is the explicit idempotency/reclaim proof.

effectAssertions: The workflow creates the exact marker effect; logs contain its sentinel; sync reports the same completed run without changing the marker.
negativeAssertions: A returned run ID without file effect, complete logs, or immutable sync state fails.
node-workflow.lifecycleAssertion: Run, log polling/follow, and sync are each bounded and timed.
node-workflow.teardownAssertion: The workflow executes only in an owned disposable sandbox removed by campaign cleanup.
node-workflow.retryAssertion: Run ID binds all read/sync retries to one execution.

effectAssertions: The node reaches the exact requested running/stopped state and preserves identity where idempotency requires it.
negativeAssertions: A host process, wrong node name, PID replacement on repeated up, or unstopped broker fails.
node-lifecycle.lifecycleAssertion: Before/after state and PID are read within bounded timeouts.
node-lifecycle.teardownAssertion: The final down-all leaves the owned sandbox broker stopped before sandbox deletion.
node-lifecycle.retryAssertion: Already-running up is the explicit idempotent no-restart proof.

effectAssertions: Every nonce-owned Relay identity is absent by bounded exact lookup.
negativeAssertions: Unknown lookup, leaked identity, baseline identity mutation, or unauthorized target fails cleanup.
cleanup-agent.lifecycleAssertion: Serial release/remove attempts and final reconciliation are timed and bounded.
cleanup-agent.retryAssertion: Cleanup retries are exact-name, ownership-gated, and idempotent.

effectAssertions: Every exact owned Daytona sandbox ID and nonce-prefixed name is absent after deletion.
negativeAssertions: Unknown ownership, refused delete, remaining ID/name, or a deleted baseline resource fails cleanup.
cleanup-sandbox.lifecycleAssertion: Each exact deletion has bounded retries/backoff and final inventory reconciliation.
cleanup-sandbox.retryAssertion: Delete is retried only for exact ledger-owned IDs and accepts already-absent as converged.

effectAssertions: All baseline sandbox/agent identities still exist and no nonce-owned resource remains.
negativeAssertions: Any missing baseline resource, exact-prefix leak, or unavailable reconciliation fails.
cleanup-baseline.lifecycleAssertion: Final inventories are captured only after exact cleanup attempts finish.
cleanup-baseline.teardownAssertion: The attempt ends only with restored baseline or INFRA_BLOCKED.
cleanup-baseline.retryAssertion: Final reconciliation is authoritative after bounded deletion retries.
